text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on November 29 in history.
1516 - Italian painter Giovanni Bellini died; he made Venice a centre of art to rival Florence.
1530 - Thomas Wolsey, English cardinal and Lord Chancellor in Henry VIII's government, died while being brought from York to London on a charge of high treason.
1543 - German painter Hans Holbein "the Younger" died of the plague. Appointed royal painter to Henry VIII, he was best known as a hugely successful portrait painter.

1780 - Maria Theresa, Holy Roman Empress, Queen of Hungary and Archduchess of Austria, died. She greatly increased the power of Austria and succeeded in curbing the worst excesses of the Catholic church.
1864 - At Sand Creek, Colorado, an army force led by Colonel John Chivington attacked and massacred at least 400 Cheyenne and Arapahoe Indians who had surrendered and been given permission to camp.
1872 - U.S. editor Horace Greeley died; he founded the daily New York Tribune in 1841.
1890 - The first Imperial Diet was opened in Japan. It consisted of a House of Peers and a House of Representatives.
1895 - U.S. choreographer Busby Berkeley born; best known for the films "Forty Second Street" and "Gold Diggers of 1933".
1902 - Italian author Carlo Levi born; famed for his story of political exile "Christ Stopped at Eboli".
1924 - Italian opera composer Giacomo Puccini, who wrote "La Boheme" and "Tosca", died; his last work "Turandot" was unfinished.
1929 - U.S. explorer Richard Byrd and Bernt Balchen completed the first flight over the South Pole.
1932 - French statesman Jacques Chirac born; prime minister in 1974 and again in 1986, he became president in 1995 succeeding Francois Mitterrand.
1939 - The USSR broke off diplomatic relations with Finland prior to the Soviet attack on the country.
1945 - The newly elected Constituent Assembly in Yugoslavia proclaimed a federal republic.
1947 - The U.N. General Assembly voted to partition Palestine into Jewish and Arab land, leading to the setting up a Jewish state the following year.
1966 - King Ntare IV was overthrown in Burundi and a republic proclaimed.
1974 - A bill to outlaw the Irish Republican Army became law in Britain.
1975 - British racing driver Graham Hill died in an air crash outside London; he had been world champion twice in 1962 and in 1968.
1981 - U.S. film actress Natalie Wood died; she was best known for her "Miracle on 34th Street" as a child star and "Bob and Carol and Ted and Alice" and "West Side Story".
1990 - Bulgarian Prime Minister Lukanov and his government resigned following a general strike
